A New Collection

Home & Roots

Virginia is home. North Carolina is roots. We drew Home & Roots from both states: the flower they share, the ridges that run through them, the light on their coasts. These are meant to hang in a house, not come home in a gift shop bag.

The motifs

Seven subjects run through the whole collection. They arrive one at a time, as wallpaper singles and as printable sets.

Dogwood

The state flower of both Virginia and North Carolina, so it had to be in here.

Blue Ridge Layers

Ridge after ridge in morning blue, the view that defines the western horizon of both states.

Shenandoah Fog

Fog sitting in the valley early, before it burns off.

Outer Banks Light

A lighthouse at golden hour on the Carolina coast.

Appalachian Quilt Geometry

The geometry of traditional hand stitched quilts, turned into pattern.

Coastal Marsh Light

Evening light over the marsh grass of the Carolina sounds.

Roots

The North Carolina ground we come from. Old homeplaces, tall pines, and the roads that still lead back there, however long we have lived away.

Home & Roots

Magnolia and Pine

Roots and Porch Light.

Magnolia and Pine is mother and son: her table, her porch light, and a son who makes things because of both.

Magnolia and Pine is the part of Home & Roots that lives at her table and under her porch light, where Virginia home and North Carolina roots meet in one room. The day pieces are magnolia in first light and a kitchen in the morning. The night pieces keep the same table and let the moon in.

For my mother, Penny, with love.

Magnolia at First Light

One magnolia branch in bloom against a warm neutral ground, with wide quiet space around the flower. The face of the collection, and the quietest picture we make.
